guides.title: Unkillable Demon Queen (Master to Low Mythic Only)
guides.description:
This guide will show you how to maximize your passives and get ahead of every lane opponent you might meet in your ranked games. Please note that this guide requires you to understand the concept of orb-walking.

Who am I?
IGN: AmyAmyAmy
Current Hanabi one trick (MM main this season), I intend to play one hero to Mythic. Fresh account. 

Current rank is Legend 4 (1 stars), 32 games, 84.38% Win Rate.
Hanabi 28 games, 85.7% WR
guides.gameplayStrategy:
Skill Order

Ultimate > Ability 1 > Ability 2


Passive: Petal Barrage

Basically this allows your auto attacks to bounce up to 4 times between any enemies (including turrets, creeps, minions & enemy heroes). The bounces do significantly less damage than the previous.


For example, if your auto attack did 100 damage, the first bounce will deal 40 damage, the second will deal 34 damage, the third will deal 29 damage and the last will deal 25 damage (40%/85%/85%/85%). This also means that each bounce is affected by Crit Damage.


Note: It won't bounce to an enemy when you hit a turret first, but can bounce from hero to turret (and back to hero), this is also important.



Ability 1: Equinox

The bread and butter for any Hanabi player. The passive on this ability allows you to be CC immune when you have a shield on (this includes shield from Turtle, your own ability, or from other heroes (e.g. Angela etc.). Upon activation you get a shield that lasts 5 seconds during which you get a boost in Movement Speed and Attack Speed. The shield size is increased when you do damage.


This is the button you press when you want to enter a fight. Since it also has a low cooldown and mana cost, you can use this ability to bait out enemy team CC/engages.



Ability 2: Soul Scroll

You shoot out some projectile that slows the enemy for 1 second, but more importantly, when you hit an enemy with this, it allows your passive to not have the damage decay



Ultimate: Higanbana

Deals damage, "stuns" enemies for 0.8 seconds and is AOE, i mean seriously, this is just broken.




Early Game:

You MUST run immediately to lane, and get into the furthest bush possible. If the enemy team in gold lane helped their jungler with the buff, tank the wave just outside the turret range and clear it asap. Since each minion wave has 3 minions, you will always get the last bounce from your passive to hit the enemy turret gold shield, giving you extra gold early on. If the enemy marksman is there with you, make sure you are in a 1v1 before going aggressive on them. Remember, even if they also took aegis, you have TWO shields. Trade with them till you are about at 20% HP, then back off to heal, as soon as you see them start to heal as well, try to hit them with your passive's bounce, if you can do this first step, the laning phase is as good as won.


Every wave possible, take the melee minion at the edge of the enemy turret range and auto attack the wave so the 4th bounce always hits the turret, this gives you an insane gold lead over your enemy marksman in the early game.


Always try to go aggressive on the enemy heroes in your lane where possible. Watch the mini map, once the roamer shows in another lane, go aggro on the enemy MM. You have a short CD shield, and a way to cancel their healing. Use it to press for early advantages.



Mid Game:

By this time you should have already taken down the outer turret. If the turtle is spawning on your side of the map, swap to the exp lane side to push that turret, if the turtle spawns on the opposite side, keep pushing waves to the outer (2nd) turret. Where possible, always tank the minions at the edge of the turret to maximize the 4th bounce on the turret.


This is the time when you are not exactly the strongest compared to other MMs so best to use skill 1 to bait out CC from the enemy or let your team mates engage first and just let the bounces kill the enemy team.


Late Game:

Lords, push waves, start fights. Turn on shield, cast ultimate, and go ham.

guides.title: Exp Lane Carmilla (or Mid Lane)
guides.description: She's so unknown as a utility Exp Laner and it definitely baffles me why she's not being played more. You can definitely play her in the Exp lane if your allies are all squishy and lacks stuns including your Roamer.
guides.gameplayStrategy:
•Items: These items are a good balance of tankiness and some damage. This build is better if the Roamer is a healer type support. If they are an Assassin type Roamer or a Mage Roamer (like Novaria) then you should consider going full tank instead.


-Anti-heal: Get Dominance Ice or Glowing Wand early if you think you need it.

-Divine Glaive: Only buy this if you really think you need the magic penetration, otherwise just consider buying one of the following: Blood Wings, Clock of Destiny, Oracle or other defensive items.

-Emblems: These emblems help you clear creep waves faster because you should be able to leave your lane fast to join teamfights since your team doesn't have a frontliner. You can also consider letting your first tower get destroyed in these type of games. It's more important for you to protect your team especially in turtle fights and if your team seems to be losing which isn't shocking since the team doesn't have a frontliner lmao. Learn to abuse lane cutting also so you can leave your lane fast.

-Battle spell: Vengeance. Revitalize or Aegis can be good and considerable if the opponents have MANY heroes that disappear and become untargettable like Lunox, Hayabusa, Kadita and Wanwan since they won't be affected by the return damage anyway. Just make sure that you have enough armor to survive Sea Halberd Damage if you do so since Vengeance was original there to also counter that item but losing it can open up the problem somehow.


••You can play Carmilla in the midlane with the same build and the same reasons + the fact that your Exp Laner picked another squishy hero without reliable CC like Zilong or Aulus for example. Heroes like Alucard or Benedetta feels like they belong in that category also, but it can depend on their build I guess.

guides.title: Fighter Cyclops
guides.description: People are still confused when they see Cyclops with Fighter Emblem and/or Queen's Wings, but the main reason that it's good and considerable is because this hero's kit involves aggression and dealing damage which can be complemented by Spell lifesteal and some tankiness.
guides.gameplayStrategy:
Core ideas of the build:

-Mana management: Inspire + Impure Rage gives you a lot of mana already so no need for Book or Clock at start. Wishing Lantern also gives you some mana and the timing in the build is perfect for when you already maxed your cooldowns. You can still run out of mana if you fight very long and consecutive clashes. There are also end-game scenarios where you should buy an emergency Book or Clock if the game is very close to ending and you don't have time to go back to base.

-Cooldown: Not 45% like the usual Cyclops Mage build. It's only 35% so you're missing 10% which isn't really a big deal and Queen's Wings reduces your skill cooldowns when triggered also.

-Anti-tank trinity: Glowing wand for anti-heal and %HP burn, Divine Glaive to counter Magic Armor and Wishing Lantern to counter High HP.

-Spell lifesteal: No Concentrated Energy like the Normal Mage build but you have some of it from the Fighter Emblem and being tanky makes that little lifesteal more valuable anyway. Normal Mage Cyclops have higher spell lifesteal but no tankiness to complement or support it. You can also just focus on thinking that more damage = more spell lifesteal.

-Armor item: Every sustain Fighter build should have at least 1 armor item so you don't get destroyed by Sea Halberd. It doesn't necessarily have to be Blade Armor but it's the only armor item that gives you some offensive tool with its return damage while significantly reducing damage from heroes with Sea Halberd.

-Other items: If you don't need Divine Glaive or an armor item, you can buy 1 or 2 of the following: Blood Wings, Concentrated Energy, Brute Force, Holy Crystal or a mana item(Lightning Truncheon is considerable too).


-Battle Spell: Possible options are Vengeance, Flame Shot and Flicker. Vengeance helps you be tankier and absorb some aggression if you want to protect a squishy teammate or if you just want to maintain the Fighter feel of the hero in general. Flame Shot is good if you really need to go fully offensive, but you should definitely consider just going back to a normal Mage build in that scenario. Flicker is more of an all-around pick, but I'd argue that Vengeance is still better most of the time and you should only get Flicker if you think you need a way to escape from heroes that creates walls like Badang and Grock.


Basically, you still get all the things you need in this build like the common Mage build but this time you are tankier and can use the hero's full potential on a different point of view. You also don't have to follow this exact sequence of itemization. You can buy Glowing Wand as first item if you need to for example. The problem with a lot of Cyclops players is their obsession with cooldowns when other tools or items are needed first. There are more possible variations to this Fighter build, but this is definitely the simplest and most straightforward variation that is closest to making Cyclops like a Fighter hero without losing much of the things he does as a pure Mage.

heroes.lore:
Born at the end of the Era of Strife, Miya bore witness to the unspeakable tragedies that befell the elves during the Endless War. She saw how the Abyss defiled the Shadow Swamp and corrupted many of her people into Dark Elves. It was not until the Moon Goddess created the Lunar Aegis over Azrya that the Moon Elves were able to thrive again under its protection. Miya became the Priestess of the Moon, and for thousands of years she served  faithfully in the Lunar Temple, diligently watching over her people. However, with the continued expansion of the Abyss and its dark legions, the Land of Dawn is once again shrouded by the fog of war. From the Moonlit Forest, a call to war that has not been heard in thousands of years sounded again. Miya took up her silver bow and swore by the light of the moon to fight for her people.

"What is war, brother?""When the races of the Land of Dawn turned on one another instead of embracing unity and mutual prosperity, that is war. When they invaded their neighbors and razed cities to the ground, that is a war. When they choose destruction over peace, cruelty over benevolence, and corruption over purity... that is war.""Peace, benevolence, and purity... is that your wish for the world?"Estes did not reply. The outstretched branches of the Tree of Life wrapped around him, and he fell back into deep slumber.This time he would not awaken again for many years. Long enough for Miya to grow from a little girl, who couldn't even reach the branches of the Tree of Life, into a fearless warrior and protector of the Moonlit Forest.

guides.title: Basic Miya Guide
guides.description: This is the basic of how to play miya
guides.gameplayStrategy:
🧩 Playstyle Tips

Early Game:

  • Focus on farming, not fighting. Miya’s early damage is mediocre.
  • Stick near turret or with a support; you’re food for assassins before core items.

Mid Game:

  • Split push when the map’s safe. Miya’s attack speed deletes turrets fast.
  • Always watch the minimap — your invisibility can dodge ganks but only if you react early.

Late Game:

  • Stay in the backline. Let tanks soak damage.
  • Wait for enemy CC skills to be used, then go in with Inspire and ult to shred them.


🧠 Quick Reminders

  • Never open fights. You finish them.
  • Manage ult carefully — it’s both escape and damage buff.
  • Positioning wins or loses every match for Miya.

guides.title: Damage dan Finisher
guides.description:
Damage tinggi, serangan cepat, sustain darah, dan kemampuan bertahan di team fight.
Ini build yang serbaguna, bisa disesuaikan ke arah “burst”, “sustain”, atau “survivability” sesuai kondisi musuh.
guides.gameplayStrategy:
STRATEGI & GAYA MAIN

  1. Early Game: Fokus farming di Gold Lane. Prioritas: sepatu → Windtalker → Fury.
  2. Mid Game: Mulai rotasi ke mid-lane untuk team fight. Jangan ragu aktifkan Ultimate untuk reposition.
  3. Late Game: Jaga posisi di belakang; pastikan Inspire/Wind of Nature selalu siap untuk fight penentuan.

Posisi Ideal: Belakang tank/fighter. Miya tidak punya skill escape selain Ultimate, jadi positioning sangat penting.

Timing Kunci: Gunakan Wind of Nature + Inspire bersamaan saat duel 1v1 melawan assassin atau marksman musuh, hasilnya hampir selalu kill.

guides.title: Balanced Silvanna Build (Exp Lane)
guides.description:
You're not meant to always win with Silvanna in lane because a lot of meta heroes are stronger than her but that's okay. Silvanna is a good "lose lane, win game" type of hero (but if you win your lane, that's great of course, and that should always be the initial goal!). 

Based on that, you should be good in playing objectives, especially in clearing waves faster, so you can join team fights since defeating your lane opponent isn't always your ultimate goal. This is the reason why Concussive Blast is always important if you ask me. Fun fact: Silvanna has the 2nd highest HP in the game at level 1 (without items and emblems) so a CB from her really deals good damage early on. The 2nd important thing is to scale defensively which is something missing in at least 90% of Silvanna builds.
guides.gameplayStrategy:
Core mentalities:

-Mage emblem + Bonus Magic damage (this also increases shield of 2nd skill) + Spell lifesteal = more survivability while still dealing good damage

-These emblems are there to balance being able to fight the opposing hero and clearing creep waves fast when needed during the laning stage. (Learn when to freeze lane or when to cut lane.)


Items:

-You can definitely change boots to Tough boots if needed. (Or Warrior boots but very rarely) 

-Only buy Divine Glaive if you truly need Magic Penetration in the exact moment or in the very near future. 

-Only buy Glowing Wand if you truly need an Anti-Heal item, otherwise just buy Blood Wings/Clock of Destiny or a Winter Crown instead. 

-Don't always autobuy Winter Crown. Check your team lineup if it's better for you to be targetable and tank damage so you can protect your squishy allies. 

-Every sustain type Fighter or builds should always have 1 armor item so you don't get destroyed by a single Sea Halberd. You should purchase the best armor item for the specific game. Even Dominance Ice is considerable which means you don't need to buy Glowing Wand in that scenario. An early Warrior boots + Dominance Ice as your first 2 items is considerable in some rare games. 

-Other anti-tank options: Wishing Lantern can work if they have 2 or more solid tank heroes. Cursed Helmet (-hybrid armor) can work if you can also utilize the tankiness that the item gives. 


-Battle Spell: Vengeance. It helps you survive and deal more damage. You can also look at your ultimate as a way of forcing the opponents into a "cage fight" which is a life-or-death situation and having Vengeance is very good there. 


••Feather of Heaven - Let's talk about this item. IT'S VERY OVERRATED. Sure, attack speed can make your 2nd skill deal more damage but just increasing your magic power in general also increases the skill's damage. Your ult also gives you a lot of attack speed already so adding more can be irrelevant. You can just get a different damage item that also gives some tankiness so you can actually do your job as an Exp laner. I'd say that this Feather of Heaven item is one of the main reasons why Silvanna doesn't feel that strong in general and why she's so low rated in Tier lists or Hero Ratings. Feather of Heaven can still be good sometimes if you really need to go hyper offensive due to your team lineup having too many tanky heroes but not enough damage output. That rarely happens though. The item is also considerable if you need do split pushing.

guides.title: Tank Emblem Diggie
guides.description: This is a tanky Diggie build that will help you stop feeding or reduce it somehow. It also helps you do a more aggressive approach for the hero which helps you utilize 2nd skill more efficiently.
guides.gameplayStrategy:
•Buy Oracle first before Magic Shoes or Flask. Reason: You should be worried about your own tankiness first and about saving yourself to avoid feeding. This way, you can also stay more in the frontlines and actually catch some damage to protect your allies (so it wasn't really a selfish approach in the first place!). This also allows Diggie to be more aggressive and be a great "fisherman" using 2nd skill.

•Battle Spell: Aegis. Again, it's for self-protection so it's better than Revitalize. You have your ult reserved to protect Allies and yourself also but don't waste it too much on yourself if possible.

•Buy 1 or 2 Magic Necklace(s) anytime you feel like you're lacking mana then sell them once you can get an Elegant Gem at least in this item build sequence.

•Ice Queen is nice cause it gives your bombs a slow debuff and makes it harder for opponents to move and come close to your team especially when you plant it on key spots where opponents may come from.

•You can buy Glowing Wand instead of Ice Queen if you think you really need the anti-heal and none of your allies bought it. You can also consider a late Dominance Ice instead.

•You need to buy 1 armor item so you don't get destroyed by Sea Halberd. If that's not an issue then just consider buying one of the following: Glowing Wand, Blood Wings or an emergency Enchanted Talisman for end-game scenarios where you run out of mana but doesn't have time to go back to base due to the game possibly ending very soon.

•Emblems: You can change Quantum Charge to Focusing Mark if there are 2 or more heroes that are very tanky in the opposing team. Focusing Mark helps kill tanky heroes especially when paired with Blue Roam Blessing debuff.

guides.title: Terizla
guides.description: How to be good at lane domination and be a effective secondary tank with massive damage dealing capacity.
guides.gameplayStrategy:
Introduction to character

Terizla is a fighter tank with a large damage dealing and soaking capabilities he can as well act as tank while dealing massive damage during team fights. His passive makes it harder for enemy to burst you down as the lower his hp gets the stronger he becomes.

Synergies

Terizla works best with roamers who can set up and mages who have large aoe damage.

He is also great with roam supports like estes, floryn and angels who can keep him alive in extended team fight

DRAFT

When ever you use terizla make sure you dont have a hard counter in enemy if enemy locks in alpha and borg avoid using him.

Early game

Terizla has a strong spell vamp and is very hard to kill but early game he can lack the proper situation to snowball. the moment you enter game priotize war axe dont go for boots. remember terizla is slow dont worry we will get boots after the war axe. unlock the 2nd skill 1st this is your main damage skill. fron the begining start ressuring lane dont over extend use your 2nd skill large area to damage all minion at once so you can still poke enemies. after reaching level 2 start kiting enemies with 1st skill make sure to hit the enemy with 1st skill rather than minnion for maximum damage. most of the fighter struggle against terizla so make sure you are ready for enemy gank.

1st turtle brawl

As being an exp laner your duty for the 1st turtle securing increases drastically so position yourself appropriately makesure your jungler is nearby before engaging and make sure you are Level 4 first if enemy are grouped very tightly that's your signal call out your roam and jungle dont engage recklessly. use your ult to lock down the grouped enemies most of them will try to escape if they dont have mobility skill 1 enemy will be pinned to ground use this to your advantage. start swinging your 2nd skill , remember you can still move when using 2nd skill so make the best out of it never auto tap your 2nd skill it makes it easy for enemy to dodge always aim and attack.

Mid game

Now dont keep sitting in your lane like a farmer rotate to other lane to help your teammate farm, the best thing about terizla is that his passive it helps you stay longer in fights so if enemy try to gank you you can survive and make the best about it.

dont engege the gank your self as its easy for enemy to dodge terizla ult if they see it coming so always try to close gap from bushes and let other use their cc on emey 1st if the enemy engages then you engage with your ult. Terizla ult knocks enemies airborne and pulls enemy to center of the slam zone giving you perfect opportunity for multiple hits with your second skill make sure either you have a roamer who can initiate or have a roamer who can support when you initiate.

Early Late Game

Early late game is where terizla shines the most as most player get thier damage items 1st and dont get defensive items it gives terizla the perfect scene his passive can soak the damage while spell vamp keeps you alive and you can get agressive during this stage. THis is the stage where terizla can dive in just with a support then come out alive with a savage but becareful terizla lacks mobility so if he gets caught in cc chain it can be difficult you might kill 1 or 2 enemy heroes but since you lance mobility reaching backline will be hard so keep and eye for enemy's chain cc. And remember keep soaking damage and keep swinging that second skill.

Late game

Once you reach late game where everyone has all items built terizla should change roles now just build a war axe and then go full tank you can use guardian helmet, twilight armour, everything that can keep you in the front line and remember to be aggressive in a full out brawl as the only way you can turn tables is by landing hits it will provide massve damage and keep you alive as well,

heroes.lore:
Alucard's father was a comrade-in-arms of Tigreal who disappeared in a battle with the Demons. Therefore, he hated darkness, joined the Monastery of Light, and swore to destory all Demons. But later he learned the hidden secrets of this battle, so he left the Monastery of Light in anger and fought the darkness in his own way.

The last great war is a glorious memory for the Moniyans. The powerful Light's Order, together with the Imperial Border Guards, wiped out the demonic strongholds at the Moniyan and the Barren Lands pass, driving the fiends back to the hinterlands of the Forsaken Wastes. But for young Alucard, the war was nothing but a terrible memory of pain and misery. His father's second regiment suffered heavy losses due to a rash lone advance. Alucard's father disappeared in the battle and was later declared dead by the Light's Order.

As they had disobeyed orders, the second regiment was not honored and praised for their sacrifice but labeled "disobedient" and criticized for their lack of discipline. This was a huge blow to Alucard, who had always regarded his father as a hero and role model. Facing shame and ridicule everywhere he went, the flames of revenge burned within his chest, and he became determined to bring honor to his father's name and eliminate all the demons in the Land of Dawn. And so, he left his hometown and journeyed to the ancient and mysterious Monastery of Light. As the orphaned son of a dead soldier, Alucard was soon accepted into the Monastery of Light.

guides.description: standart jungle alucard
guides.gameplayStrategy:
Early Game:

  • Focus heavily on farming (jungle camps or lane minions depending on your role). Alucard is weak early.
  • Don’t force fights unless you’re sure you win (target isolated enemy, minimal risk).
  • Take red buff / buff camps to boost your clear if in jungle.

Mid Game:

  • You should have some key items, begin ganking, rotating, helping your team secure objectives (Turtle, Lord) and pushing lanes.
  • Use your combo: leap in, use area damage, activate ultimate, follow up.
  • Target squishy enemies or catch enemies out of position.

Late Game:

  • You become a major threat. But positioning is crucial: don’t go first into full chaos unless you have backup.
  • Use your ult in key moment – finishing off low HP enemies, diving safely.
  • Push towers when safe; you can also steal jungle camps or buff from enemy if you’re ahead.

guides.title: Yin the Isolator: A Burst Jungler Guide to Destroying the Enemy Carry
guides.description: Yin is a Fighter/Assassin hero with a unique mechanic to isolate an enemy target and destroy them in a 1v1 duel within his own domain. With the right build, you will become a fearsome burst damage dealer, dreaded by vulnerable enemy heroes like Marksman, Mage, Assassin, and Support. Imagine ambushing from the grass, dragging the enemy's main carry into your personal dimension, and eliminating them in seconds before the enemy team can even react.
guides.gameplayStrategy:
⚙️ Build Specifications

A. Battle Spell

The Battle Spell used is Retribution (for Jungler only), with the blessing:

  • Flame Retribution (Red) – Steals Physical Attack and Magic Power from enemies. This is perfect for increasing your burst damage in 1v1 fights, especially inside your ultimate's domain, ensuring the target dies instantly.
  • Ice Retribution (Blue) – Steals enemy Movement Speed. This is a great choice if the enemy team has many agile heroes that are hard to catch, helping you to approach or chase them.


B. Main Emblem & Talents

Emblem:

  • Assassin – Provides high Adaptive Penetration and Movement Speed.


Talent:

  1. Rupture – Provides additional Adaptive Penetration.
  2. Weapon Master – Increases the Physical Attack and Magic Power gained from equipment, emblems, and skills.
  3. Quantum Charge – Restores HP and increases Movement Speed when dealing damage with a basic attack.


C. Alternative Emblem & Talents

Talent:

[ Talent 1 ]

  • Thrill – Provides additional Adaptive Attack.

[ Talent 2 ]

  • Master Assassin – Increases damage to lone enemy heroes.
  • Seasoned Hunter – Increases damage to Jungle Monsters (Creep), Turtle, and Lord.

[ Talent 3 ]

  • Lethal Ignition – Deals extra burst damage after a multi-hit combo.
  • Killing Spree – Restores a percentage of HP and grants a bonus to Movement Speed after dealing damage to a hero with a skill when at low HP.


D. Core Items

  1. Magic Shoes – Provides cooldown reduction.
  2. Blade of Heptaseas – The core burst item. Provides Physical Penetration and extra physical damage.
  3. Sky Piercer – Executes enemies with low HP.
  4. Endless Battle – Provides True Damage and HP restoration.
  5. Blade of Despair – Significantly increases Physical Attack.
  6. Malefic Roar – Provides high Physical Penetration.


E. Situational Items

  • Tough Boots – Reduces the duration of crowd control effects.
  • Rose Gold Meteor – Grants a shield to protect against magic burst damage.
  • Sea Halberd – Reduces the enemy's healing and regeneration effects.
  • Immortality – Provides extra protection in the late game and a second life after being burst down.


⌕ See more about this build.


🎯 Micro Analysis: Understanding Yin's Kit

A. Passive: Leave It To Me

  • Description: Yin gains 120% increased damage and 8% Spell Vamp when there are no teammates nearby. The minimum distance between Yin and a teammate to activate this passive is 4 units. This passive is inactive when Yin is within the domain.
  • Gameplay Implication: With this passive, Yin is highly suited for 1v1 fights. You must play selfish and often go solo to utilize this passive. Avoid being near allies if unnecessary, especially while farming or dueling.


B. Skill Breakdown

Skill 1: Charged Punch

  • Yin gains 60% increased Movement Speed and enhanched Basic Attack. When the enhanched Basic Attack hits an enemy, Yin throws a Charged punch forward, dealing massive damage to the enemy. When Yin successfully lands the Charged punch, it reduces the cooldown of this skill by 35%. With this skill, Yin can more easily chase enemies or escape from pursuit.

Skill 1: Frenzy Strike (Lieh Mode)

  • Lieh strikes the area in front of him 10 times, each strike dealing high damage to enemies and applying a Slow effect. Lieh becomes immune to crowd control effects for the duration. The striking speed increases gradually.

Skill 2: Instant Blast

  • Yin dashes forward, leaving a Golden Ring behind while dealing damage to enemies along the path. Yin gains damage reduction if an enemy hero is hit. After 1 second, the Golden Ring returns to Yin, dealing damage to enemies it passes through and Stun them for 1 second.

Skill 2: Instant Blast (Lieh Mode)

  • Lieh kicks forward, leaving a Golden Ring behind, dealing damage to enemies along the path. Enemies hit are slightly Knockback and receive 25% damage reduction for 4 seconds if an enemy hero is hit. After 1 second, the Golden Ring returns to Lieh, dealing damage to enemies it passes through and Stun them for 1.25 seconds.

Ultimate: My Turn

  • Yin pulls an enemy hero into his domain or arena for 8 seconds and transforms into Lieh Mode. While inside the domain, both heroes cannot be affected by any other heroes' skills. Lieh possesses stronger skills and gains extra Physical Defense and Magic Defense. The domain ends early if one of the heroes is eliminated. If Lieh successfully kills the enemy hero, he restores a portion of his lost HP, leaves the area with his non-ultimate skill cooldowns reset, and remains in Lieh Mode for 8 seconds.


C. Types of Yin Combos

1. Ganking/Quick Burst Combo

  • Sequence: Skill 1 → Skill 2 → Basic Attack → Ultimate → Skill 2 → Skill 1
  • When to Use & Its Use: To eliminate priority targets (Marksman, Mage, Assassin, Support). This is the standard ganking combo. The Stun from Skill 2 is the key to ensuring the Ultimate doesn't miss.

2. Laning/Poke Combo

  • Sequence: Skill 1 → Skill 2 → Basic Attack
  • When to Use & Its Use: In the early laning phase, or when the target is too far away. Use Skill 1 to chase/deal damage, and Skill 2 to Stun. If the target doesn't die, you still have your Ultimate as a backup.

3. Maximum Burst Combo

  • Sequence: Skill 1 → Skill 2 → Basic Attack → Ultimate → Skill 2 → Flame Retribution + Skill 1
  • When to Use & Its Use: To secure a kill inside the domain against tough enemies (Tank, Fighter). Flame Retribution is used inside the domain to increase Yin's damage.

4. Chase Combo

  • Sequence: Skill 1 → Basic Attack
  • When to Use & Its Use: Chasing a fleeing or low HP enemy. Use the mobility from Skill 1 (Charged Punch) to chase or escape.

5. Bush Ambush Combo

  • Sequence: Skill 2 → Skill 1 → Basic Attack → Ultimate → Skill 2 → Skill 1
  • When to Use & Its Use: A surprise attack from within a bush. Start with Skill 2 for a sudden Stun, then continue with the standard combo.


🗺️ Macro Analysis: Strategy per Game Phase

A. Yin's Identity in the Game

Yin's identity is that of "The Lone Hunter" or "The Duelist". Therefore, your entire macro strategy must revolve around:

  1. Utilizing the Passive "Leave It To Me". You MUST play selfish. The presence of teammates actually weakens you. Prioritize walking/rotating alone, farming alone, and creating 1v1 situations.
  2. Using the Ultimate "My Turn" as a Macro Tool. Your ultimate is not just a damage skill, but a tool for controlling the game. Its primary functions are:
  • Removing One Threat – Taking the enemy's damage dealer out of the teamfight.
  • Creating a Number Advantage – By locking down one enemy, your team fights 4 vs 4.5 (because the enemy in the domain cannot help). If you win, it becomes 5 vs 4.
  • Securing Objectives – Ensuring the enemy cannot steal the Turtle/Lord or hinder a push by reducing their number of heroes.


B. Macro Strategy per Game Phase

🕛 Early Game Phase (Minutes 1-4): The Silent Farmer

Main Objective: Reach Level 4 as quickly as possible and get your first core item (Blade of Heptaseas).

Strategy:

  1. Start at the Buff: Begin with the nearest buff. Use Retribution immediately. Utilize your passive to clear the jungle with full HP.
  2. Full Clear & Isolate: Clear the entire jungle on your first side. DO NOT call your Tank/Roamer to help you clear! Remember, your passive is only active when there are no teammates nearby. If the roamer approaches, give the "Retreat" signal.
  3. Powerspike at Level 4: This is your most critical moment. Upon reaching Level 4, look at the minimap and determine which lane is the easiest to gank.

First Ganking Priorities:

  • Gold Lane (Marksman Lane). The best target. Killing the enemy Marksman early game severely disrupts their farm and progress.
  • Lane with a low HP enemy or one without blink/Flicker.
  • Lane that is over-extended (pushed too far forward).


🕒 Mid Game Phase (Minutes 5-15): The Prime Hunter

Main Objective: Build a "snowball" (consecutive advantage), control the map, and dominate objectives.

Strategy:

  1. Pick-Off & Rotation: This phase is your peak power spike. You must not be idle. Continuously rotate to look for "pick-offs" (killing a lone target). Use the "Ganking/Quick Burst Combo".
  2. Objective Control (Turtle/Lord): Before the Turtle or Lord spawn, create a favorable situation by: killing the enemy Jungler or Damage Dealer — his is the safest way to secure the objective or forcing the enemy to recall through aggressive ganking, so they cannot be present in the objective area.
  3. Split Push & Pressure: Yin is a decent split-pusher. If the team is in a deadlock, push a different lane. If one enemy comes to stop you, assess their strength. If they are a target you can kill (Marksman, Mage, Assassin, Support), use your Ultimate and eliminate them. If they are a strong Fighter/Tank, use Skill 1 or Skill 2 to escape.
  4. Vision Play: Always monitor the minimap to track the position of the enemy carry. Avoid areas without vision because you are susceptible to ambushes.


🕘 Late Game Phase (Minutes 15+): The Cunning Assassin

Main Objective: Close the game or win the decisive teamfight. One mistake can be fatal.

Strategy:

  1. Mindset Shift: You are no longer as powerful as you were in the mid game. Enemies have defensive items (Immortality, Wind of Nature, Antique Cuirass). You must become the "Clean-Up Crew", not the initiator.
  2. Patience is Key: In a teamfight, do not engage first. Hide in a bush or on the flank (the side). Wait until the enemy's main crowd control (CC) and burst skills have been used.
  3. Strict Target Selection: Engage only when you are 100% certain you can eliminate the priority target. It is better to wait 5 seconds longer than to pull a Tank and die pointlessly. Use the "Maximum Burst Combo" to secure the kill inside your domain.


C. Combo Application in a Macro Context

1. Ganking/Quick Burst Combo

  • Used for: Standard ganking in the early/mid game, when targets are still relatively "squishy".
  • Macro Context: You use it when rotating to kill a target who is alone in a lane or in the enemy jungle.

2. Maximum Burst Combo

  • Used for: More tanky targets (e.g., an Assassin with Antique Cuirass), or in the late game when every kill is extremely valuable.
  • Macro Context: Used in "all-in" situations where you must secure the kill, such as during a Lord fight or in a decisive teamfight. Using Flame Retribution inside the domain is key.

3. Chase Combo

  • Used for: Chasing a low HP enemy, or escaping.
  • Macro Context: After winning a teamfight, use this to chase down remaining fleeing enemies. Also used for "hit-and-run" tactics while split-push.


D. ⚠️ Important Macro Tips

  • Communicate with Your Team. Communicate your ultimate target. Inform your team so they are ready to follow-up.
  • Counter Enemy Builds. If a priority target builds Wind of Nature or Winter Crown, WAIT for their active effects to expire before using your Ultimate or full combo.
  • Don't Force Plays. If a gank fails or your team loses a fight, do not be reckless. Return to farming. Yin is highly dependent on items. An unnecessary death will halt your momentum.


⛔️ Common Mistakes Players Make When Using Yin & How to Fix Them

1. Wrong Ultimate Target: Pulling a Tank/Fighter into the Domain

  • Mistake: Using your ultimate on a Tank hero like Tigreal or a sustain Fighter like Yu Zhong.
  • Consequence: You cannot kill them within 8 seconds. You waste your Ultimate, and your teamfights a 4v4 without their jungler.
  • Solution: FOCUS. Only prioritize ultimating Marksman, Mage, Assassin, or Support (squishy hero). Use the target lock feature (the target icon above the skill) to ensure you don't hit the wrong target.

2. Staying Too Close to Teammates, Wasting the Passive

  • Mistake: Always grouping with the team, especially when farming or dueling in the early game.
  • Consequence: The passive "Leave It To Me" is not active. You lose the bonus damage and Spell Vamp, resulting in slow jungle clears, weak duels, and rapid HP loss.
  • Solution: Play selfish. Farm and rotate alone. When the team is about to engage in a 5v5, position yourself on the flank so your passive remains active before you dive in to attack the enemy carry.

3. Engaging Too Early in a Teamfight (Initiator)

  • Mistake: Dash with Skill 2 directly into the enemy crowd to start the fight.
  • Consequence: Yin built with damage items is very squishy. You will be instantly melted by enemy crowd control and burst damage before you can even use your Ultimate.
  • Solution: Be patient. Wait for your team's initiator (Roamer/EXP Laner) to start the fight. Wait until the enemy's main crowd control and burst skills (like Eudora or Aurora Ultimate) have been used. Only then should you enter from the flank (the side) to pick-off your prey.

4. Forcing a Play After a Failed Gank

  • Mistake: After missing the stun from Skill 2 (Instant Blast), the player still forces their way in by charging forward or using their Ultimate.
  • Consequence: Without the initial stun, it is very easy for the enemy to avoid Yin's Ultimate with Flicker or a dash/blink skill. You will be left vulnerable and easily killed.
  • Solution: If your Skill 2 misses, read the situation. If it's not feasible, retreat immediately. Return to the jungle to farm and wait for your skill cooldown. Look for another opportunity. A failed gank is better than a death.

5. Not Paying Attention to Enemy Active Items

  • Mistake: Immediately using your Ultimate or full combo on a Marksman who has Wind of Nature or a Mage who has built Winter Crown.
  • Consequence: The target uses their active item, becomes immune, and survives your domain/full combo. Your used skills are wasted, and you are left in a dangerous position.
  • Solution: Wait and bait. Keep track of enemy battle spells and active items. If they have already used Wind of Nature or Winter Crown, then use your Ultimate/full combo. Alternatively, just apply pressure to make them panic and use their item first.

6. Rigid Builds That Are Not Situational

  • Mistake: Always building full damage items without considering the enemy team composition.
  • Consequence: If the enemy team has high magic burst damage (like Eudora) or strong physical damage, you will die instantly before you can make an impact.
  • Solution: Learn to adapt. Do not hesitate to sell one damage item to counter the enemy, putting yourself in a more advantageous position.

7. Forgetting That They Can Be Crowd-Controlled While Trying to Cast Their Ultimate

  • Mistake: Assuming Yin is immune CC when casting his Ultimate.
  • Consequence: You cast your ultimate in front of an enemy who still has a crowd control (Stun, Suppress) skill, and your channeling is canceled. The pulling process of Yin's Ultimate can be interrupted by crowd control (Stun, Suppress). If you are hit by CC while aiming the Ultimate, the skill will be canceled.
  • Solution: Ensure you have stunned the target with Skill 2 first before using your Ultimate. This is the safest guarantee to prevent your Ultimate from being canceled.

8. Slow Farming in the Early Game Due to Fear of Dying

  • Mistake: Being too passive in the early game, afraid to invade or contest the Lithowanderer because you feel Yin is weak.
  • Consequence: Your development is slow, your Level 4 powerspike is delayed, and you lose the momentum to snowball.
  • Solution: Utilize your passive and Retribution. Yin has good duel potential at levels 1-3 thanks to his passive. Do not hesitate to contest the Lithowanderer or even invade if you see the enemy jungler appearing on the opposite lane.


By studying Yin's macro and micro, applying this strategy, and aligning it with your combo, you will play Yin not only as a powerful hero, but as a smart player who can control the flow of the game.


— Greetings from player MLBB Indonesia 🇮🇩

heroes.lore:
Fanny is the younger sister of Tigreal, who grew up under the protection of her family and her elder brother since she was a child. But Tigreal took the blame for a mistake in battle and left home. Disregarding obstructions from her family, Fanny joined the army, and through her own designed weapons, she successfully completed one task after another, becoming an outstanding fighter who can take care of herself.

Fanny Wertz is the youngest daughter of the Wertz family and the youngest sister of Tigreal. Although the men of the Wertz family served in the army for generations and guarded the Moniyan Empire, the female members of the family were never allowed to join the army. From the perspective of the men in the family, their duty was to protect the country and family from threats, and women were to stay away from war.

Therefore, ever since she was a child, Fanny had been asked to study painting and design art. The elders of the family hoped that she could become a famous artist or designer, and help manage the family’s business. But Fanny regarded this as beneath her. From ever since she could remember, Tigreal was Fanny’s greatest hero. She also hoped that one day, like her brother, she could fight on the front lines for the Imperial Army and guard the empire.

As the oldest noble in the Empire, House Baroque ruled over Castle Gorge. The eldest son of Duke Baroque—Lancelot was a handsome young man with [unmatched] sword skills. He'd received an all-round good education but also inherited his father's snobbery and haughtiness.

House Baroque had been in decline for years, and the duke was relying on loans to keep up a [façade]. To revive his family, the duke came up with a brilliant plan—to choose a daughter-in-law with a handsome dowry and make a fortune out of Lancelot's marriage. Or so he thought…
